chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele at rs6983267 in HCT 116; loss of binding on alt T derepresses POU5F1B in colon and increases colorectal cancer risk

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele at rs6983267. E07 shows a TCF7L2 ENCODE ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in HCT 116, but does not itself resolve allelic binding; the ref-G-more direction is inferred from E08, in which alt T is associated with higher POU5F1B expression, under a model where TCF7L2 binding at G represses POU5F1B. QBiC-SELEX coverage for TCF7L2 is not_checked: no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup was supplied, and E07 is ChIP-seq, not QBiC-SELEX.

rs6983267 lies in proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 with DNase, H3K27ac and CTCF signal, and the HCT 116 TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak overlaps this region. This supports enhancer localization and TCF7L2 occupancy, not allele-specific enhancer activity.

POU5F1B is 78.9 kb from its TSS, is the best L2G gene across credible sets at 0.89, and is a TWAS candidate; however, the listed L2G credible sets are mostly prostate cancer/PSA, not colorectal cancer. GTEx Colon-Transverse reports NES +0.20 for the alt T allele on POU5F1B expression. This links the allele to POU5F1B expression in colon but does not prove this enhancer targets POU5F1B.

HCT 116 is the stated expression context and E07 provides HCT 116 TCF7L2 ChIP-seq occupancy at the variant-containing peak. E09 shows POU5F1B is not essential in HCT 116 (gene effect -0.09) and 0% of bowel lineage lines are dependent, so cell-type-specific essentiality support is limited.

The strongest colorectal cancer GWAS record has effect allele T (p 2.0e-122), matching alt T higher POU5F1B expression, and E06d reports that POU5F1B fosters colorectal cancer proliferation and metastatic potential. Direction is not uniform across all E04 colon records, and E09 weakens the HCT 116 essentiality component, so the phenotype link is association plus literature, not proof of mediation.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP in HCT 116 will show more ref G than alt T occupancy at rs6983267.
In colon or HCT 116, alt T will associate with higher POU5F1B expression, consistent with E08 NES +0.20, because loss of TCF7L2 binding derepresses POU5F1B.
POU5F1B perturbation will affect colorectal cancer phenotypes in at least some contexts, although E09 predicts little effect in HCT 116 itself.
falsified_if: No allele-specific TCF7L2 binding is seen at rs6983267 in colorectal cells.
POU5F1B expression is not allele-dependent in colon or HCT 116.
The enhancer does not contact or regulate POU5F1B.
POU5F1B loss has no colorectal cancer phenotype in contexts where the chain claims it does.

chains.title: No TCF7L2-mediated allelic effect at rs6983267; the association reflects a linked causal variant, haplotype context, or no functional difference at this base
predictions: No reproducible allele-specific TCF7L2 binding at rs6983267 in colorectal cells.
The E08 POU5F1B colon eQTL is explained by a linked variant or 8q24 haplotype rather than this base change.
Enhancer reporter or CRISPR allele-swap shows no TCF7L2-dependent allelic effect on POU5F1B, MYC, CCAT2 or PCAT1.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TCF7L2 binding plus an enhancer-reporter difference and a target-gene change are demonstrated for rs6983267.

chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele at rs6983267 and alters MYC expression in colorectal cells, promoting colorectal cancer

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt T allele at rs6983267. E07 supports TCF7L2 occupancy in a variant-containing HCT 116 ChIP-seq peak but not allele specificity; the ref-G-more direction is inferred, not directly shown. QBiC-SELEX coverage for TCF7L2 is not_checked.

rs6983267 lies in proximal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3858447 with DNase, H3K27ac and CTCF signal, and the HCT 116 TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak overlaps it. This is enhancer localization and occupancy, not allele-specific activity.

MYC is 334.4 kb upstream of the variant. This is proximity only; E08 reports a significant colon eQTL only for POU5F1B, not MYC, so there is no direct variant-MYC expression link in the supplied evidence.
HCT 116 is the stated expression context and E07 shows TCF7L2 ChIP-seq occupancy in HCT 116, but no HCT 116 MYC expression, contact or perturbation evidence links this element to MYC.

rs6983267 is associated with colorectal cancer and colon phenotypes. The strongest colorectal cancer record has effect allele T, while several colon PheCode records have effect allele G; the phenotype link is association-level and direction is not uniform.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP in HCT 116 will show more ref G than alt T occupancy at rs6983267.
MYC expression or enhancer-MYC contact will differ by allele in colorectal cells.
MYC perturbation will attenuate the allele-dependent colorectal cancer phenotype.

MYC expression or enhancer-MYC contact is not allele-dependent in colorectal cells.
MYC perturbation does not affect the allele-dependent phenotype.

checks.why: Directly tests whether TCF7L2 actually binds at rs6983267 in HCT 116; this is the shared core missing link for H1, H2 and H3.
Tests whether rs6983267 is a colon eQTL for POU5F1B, and secondarily MYC, CCAT2 or PCAT1; this would separate H1 vs H2/H3 target-gene rankings.
Tests whether POU5F1B is functionally required in colorectal cancer lineage, which would strengthen or weaken the H2 gene-to-phenotype step.

In the post-GWAS analyses, we first identified new genome-wide significant associations: three genomic risk loci were identified at 8q24.21 (rs6983267, P = 6.98 × 10-12), 15q13.3 (rs58658771, P = 1.40 × 10-10), and 18q21.1 (rs6507874, P = 1.91 × 10-14).

In addition, the TWAS also identified four loci statistically significantly associated with CRC risk, largely explained by expression regulation, including six candidate genes (DUSP10, POU5F1B, C11orf53, COLCA1, COLCA2, and GREM1-AS1).

Here, upon characterizing cancer-specific transposable element-driven transpochimeric gene transcripts (TcGTs) produced by this tumor in the SYSCOL cohort, we find that expression of the hominid-restricted retrogene POU5F1B through aberrant activation of a primate-specific endogenous retroviral promoter is a strong negative prognostic biomarker.
Correlating this observation, we demonstrate that POU5F1B fosters the proliferation and metastatic potential of CRC cells.
